mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-inflation spike window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.5 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In a sample of 20 such labor strength events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% inflation-adjusted growth for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand, which elevates equity risk premia and produces positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 50 such demand acceleration events, 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (mean <= 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a sharp rise in consumer confidence (HOUST) suggests supply-side constraints and shifting risk perceptions, jointly pushing 20-day S&P 500 returns to the negative.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% while HOUST rises by > 20 points in the same month
regime_hint: supply disruption coupled with elevated confidence
failure_condition: In 30 such events, 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, the discount rate for future cash flows is expected to decline, enhancing equity valuation and producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: During 10 such rate easing phases, 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 30-day pre-easing period average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining labor participation rate proxies (not available in the given catalog) would be a counterfactual here, but instead, a sustained rise in job openings (not available) is replaced by a high PAYEMS coupled with a rising UNRATE, suggesting labor market saturation and a bearish 20-day S&P 500 return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS remains above 130,000 for 4 consecutive months while UNRATE stays above 7%
failure_condition: In 15 saturation events, 20-day returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a high-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL > 6% for 3 months) reduces the real present value of equity returns, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns regardless of other signals.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL exceeds 6% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During 8 such inflation spikes, 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of FEDFUNDS above 6% with no material change in industrial production (INDPRO) creates a risk-off environment where 60-day S&P 500 forward returns turn negative as investors discount future cash flows more heavily.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 6% for two consecutive months and INDPRO remains flat for the same period
failure_condition: In 12 such risk-off events, 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1).
